gloss: introduction; preface (of a thesis or essay)

definitions.explanation: The opening section of a thesis, essay, or academic work that presents the topic, purpose, and scope. Used primarily in academic and formal writing contexts.

examples.japanese: {論文|ろんぶん}の{序論|じょろん}で{研究|けんきゅう}の{目的|もくてき}を{述|の}べた。
examples.english: I stated the purpose of the research in the introduction of the thesis.

examples.japanese: {序論|じょろん}・{本論|ほんろん}・{結論|けつろん}の{三|さん}つに{分|わ}けて{書|か}きなさい。
examples.english: Write it divided into three parts: introduction, main body, and conclusion.

examples.japanese: この{本|ほん}の{序論|じょろん}だけでも{読|よ}む{価値|かち}がある。
examples.english: Even just the introduction of this book is worth reading.

notes:
Composed of {序|じょ} (preface, order) and {論|ろん} (argument, essay). Refers specifically to the introductory section of an academic paper or formal essay, where the writer sets out the background, purpose, and scope of the work.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {序論|じょろん}を{書|か}く: to write an introduction
- {論文|ろんぶん}の{序論|じょろん}: thesis introduction
- {序論|じょろん}・{本論|ほんろん}・{結論|けつろん}: introduction, body, conclusion

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {序文|じょぶん}: preface, foreword — written by the author before the main text; less academic than {序論|じょろん}
- {前書|まえが}き: foreword, preface — a more casual opening note
- {導入|どうにゅう}: introduction — broader term; can also mean introducing a system or concept, not just a written section
- イントロ: intro — casual loanword abbreviation, often used for music
